Entry 5 – 15 Jan 2026, 11.30 am
Contacted the microfilm lab regarding the condition of MF/SS/1872-01. The lab confirmed that the reel has been scheduled for digitization in Feb 2026, but the original will remain available for viewing until then. I have placed a hold on the reel for Ms. Lim’s use on 16 Jan (morning session).

Entry 6 – 15 Jan 2026, 3.40 pm
Received a call from Ms. Lim. She asked whether the 1872 entry includes any notation about the family’s religion or the name of the attending midwife. I checked the original entry again; the column headers on the 1872 form are: No., Name, Sex, Date of Birth, Place of Birth, Father’s Name, Mother’s Name, and Remarks. She said she will follow up with a separate request for the 1888–1900 registers if needed.
Ms. Lim mentioned in her earlier call that the family story says they lived in a shophouse near the Singapore River for many years. A move from Kampong Bahru Road to Upper Hokkien Street between 1872 and 1887 is plausible, but I have no primary source to confirm the timing. I will note this in the summary I plan to send her next week.

---

**Entry 10 – 17 Jan 2026, 9.50 am**
Requested the death records for Lim Chye Guan from the National Archives of Singapore. The death registers for 1931 are held in series R/1931, with microfilm copies available. The relevant reel is MF/SS/1931-02, which covers the period January to June 1931. I have placed a hold on this reel for viewing on 20 Jan (morning session).

The archive’s online catalogue shows an entry under “Lim Chye Guan” in the 1931 death index (series I/1931, page 14). The index card reads:

- Reg. no. 1931/0247
- Name: Lim Chye Guan
- Date of death: 14 Mar 1931
- Age: 58 years (calculated, based on reported birth year 1872)
- Place of death: 21 Upper Hokkien Street
- Cause of death: (illegible on index card; to be verified from register)
- Informant: Lim Ah Kow, son, same address

The age of 58 is consistent with a birth in 1872, assuming the informant’s report is accurate. I will verify the exact age and cause of death from the register itself.

---

**Entry 11 – 17 Jan 2026, 11.20 am**
While waiting for the death register reel, I searched the archive’s online database for any other records under “Lim Chye Guan” or variants. Results:

- 1872 birth (reg. no. 1872/0078) – confirmed
- 1887 entry (reg. no. 1887/0217) – likely the same person, but address differs; to be confirmed
- 1931 death (reg. no. 1931/0247) – confirmed from index

No marriage record found under this name. The 1887 entry may be a marriage or a registry of some other event; I will pull the full entry when I next visit the reading room.

---

**Entry 12 – 17 Jan 2026, 3.05 pm**
Prepared a draft summary of findings so far for Ms. Lim. The draft includes the confirmed birth record, the pending death record, and the unresolved address question. I will finalise the summary after I view the 1931 register.

I also noted that the 1931 index card lists the informant as Lim Ah Kow, son. This is the same name as the person in the 1872 birth register entry immediately before our subject (reg. no. 1872/0077). This may be a coincidence, but it could also indicate a family connection. I will check the 1872 entry for Lim Ah Kow’s father’s name when I next have the reel out.

---

**Entry 13 – 20 Jan 2026, 9.15 am**
Viewed reel MF/SS/1931-02 at the microfilm lab. The reel is in good condition. The death register entry for reg. no. 1931/0247 reads:

- Name: Lim Chye Guan
- Sex: Male
- Date of death: 14 Mar 1931
- Place of death: 21 Upper Hokkien Street, Singapore
- Cause of death: Senile decay (as reported by informant)
- Informant: Lim Ah Kow, son, 21 Upper Hokkien Street
- Date of registration: 16 Mar 1931
- Remarks: (blank)

The entry is clean and legible. The cause of death is listed as “senile decay,” which is consistent with the reported age of 58–59, though the term is broad and was commonly used for older adults in the period.

Lim Chye Guan's death_year is recorded as 1931 in the archival records. Record status: current.

---

**Entry 14 – 20 Jan 2026, 10.30 am**
Photographed the death register page (frame 9, page 41) at 600 dpi. Saved as `G:\LimFamily\1931\DeathReg_1931-0247.tif`. A JPEG preview was emailed to Ms. Lim at 10.45 am. She replied at 11.
The father’s name matches our subject. The address is the same street but a different number (18 vs. 21). This strengthens the hypothesis that Lim Ah Kow (the informant on the 1931 death entry) is the son of our subject. The address difference may simply reflect a family move between 1872 and 1931, or the numbering of Upper Hokkien Street may have changed. I will note this in the summary.

Photographed the page (frame 14, page 37) at 600 dpi. Saved as `G:\LimFamily\1872\BirthReg_1872-0077.tif`.

---

**Entry 16 – 22 Jan 2026, 3.45 pm**

Checked the 1887 entry (reg. no. 1887/0217) that was flagged earlier. I pulled the register reel MF/SS/1887-01. The entry reads:

- Name: Lim Chye Guan
- Sex: Male
- Event type: Marriage
- Date of event: 3 Aug 1887
- Place of event: 21 Upper Hokkien Street, Singapore
- Groom’s father: Lim Ah Kow (deceased)
- Bride: Chua Neo
- Bride’s father: Chua Kim Seng (deceased)
- Witnesses: Lim Peng Soon, Tan Kim Chwee
- Date of registration: 10 Aug 1887

This is a marriage record, not a birth or death. The address matches the 1931 death entry (21 Upper Hokkien Street). The groom’s father is listed as Lim Ah Kow, deceased. This is a different Lim Ah Kow from the one born in 1872 (who would have been only 15 in 1887). The name is common, so this may be an unrelated family or a different branch. The bride’s name matches the mother in the 1872 birth entry, which suggests this is indeed our subject’s marriage to Chua Neo. The 1872 birth of Lim Ah Kow (son) predates the marriage by 15 years, which is unusual but not impossible if the couple married later in life or if the 1872 birth was from a prior union. I will flag this for Ms. Lim and suggest she verify with family oral history.

Photographed the page (frame 22, page 58). Saved as `G:\LimFamily\1887\MarriageReg_1887-0217.tif`.

---

The Straits Settlements Records record_series_number is SSR-1888-01. Record status: current.

**Entry 17 – 23 Jan 2026, 10.10 am**

Compiled a comparison table for the three Lim Chye Guan records found so far:

| Record type | Reg. no. | Date | Address | Notes |
|-------------|----------|------|---------|-------|
| Birth (subject) | 1872/0078 | 11 Nov 1872 | 18 Upper Hokkien St | Father: Lim Ah Kow (deceased) |
| Marriage | 1887/0217 | 3 Aug 1887 | 21 Upper Hokkien St | Groom’s father: Lim Ah Kow (deceased) |
| Death | 1931/0247 | 14 Mar 1931 | 21 Upper Hokkien St | Informant: Lim Ah Kow, son |

The address progression (18 → 21) is consistent with a move sometime between 1872 and 1887. The father’s name in the 1872 birth entry is Lim Ah Kow, which matches the groom’s father in the 1887 marriage entry. This suggests a naming pattern: the father and the son share the same name (Lim Ah Kow), which is common in the period. I will note this in the summary for Ms. Lim.

---

**Entry 18 – 23 Jan 2026, 11.30 am**

Drafted the final summary for Ms. Lim. Key findings:

1. Confirmed birth record: reg. no. 1872/0078, dated 11 Nov 1872, at 18 Upper Hokkien Street.
2. Confirmed death record: reg. no. 1931/0247, dated 14 Mar 1931, at 21 Upper Hokkien Street.
3. Marriage record found: reg. no. 1887/0217, dated 3 Aug 1887, at 21 Upper Hokkien Street.
4. The 1887 address matches the 1931 death address, suggesting the family remained at 21 Upper Hokkien Street for over 40 years.
5. The father’s name in the 1872 birth entry (Lim Ah Kow, deceased) matches the groom’s father in the 1887 marriage entry, confirming a family naming pattern.
**Entry 19 – 23 Jan 2026, 2.15 pm**

Ms. Lim called back after receiving my draft. She confirmed the family oral history that Lim Ah Kow (the father) had a first wife who passed away in the 1860s, and that the 1872 birth was from that first marriage. This resolves the age gap concern. The son, also named Lim Ah Kow, was born 1872 and later became the informant on the 1931 death record. I will update the summary to note that the naming pattern is deliberate, likely to continue the grandfather's name.

---

**Entry 20 – 24 Jan 2026, 9.40 am**

Started searching for immigration records for the Lim family. The family likely arrived in Singapore in the 1850s or 1860s. Checked the Straits Settlements Records index for passenger lists. Found a reference to a "Lim Ah Kow" arriving on the ship *S.S. Singapore* on 12 Mar 1865. The index entry is SSR-1865-014, series 4, item 22. I will request the full manifest from the archives.

Also noted that the National Archives has a separate collection of Chinese Protectorate records. These may contain additional immigration or registration details for the family. I will check the index for "Lim" entries in that series as well.

---

**Entry 21 – 24 Jan 2026, 11.05 am**

Requested the manifest for SSR-1865-014. The archives staff said the digitized copy is available. Downloaded the image: `G:\LimFamily\1865\Manifest_1865-014.tif`. The manifest lists passengers on the *S.S. Singapore* departing from Amoy (Xiamen) on 28 Feb 1865 and arriving in Singapore on 12 Mar 1865.

The entry for Lim Ah Kow is on line 34, page 2. The record shows:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Name | Lim Ah Kow |
| Age | 28 |
| Occupation | Labourer |
| Place of origin | Amoy, Fujian |
| Destination | Singapore |
| Remarks | None |

The age of 28 in 1865 suggests a birth year of approximately 1837. This is consistent with the father being in his mid-30s at the time of the 1872 birth. I will note this as supporting evidence for the father's identity.

---

**Entry 22 – 24 Jan 2026, 2.30 pm**

The manifest for SSR-1865-014 also lists a "Lim Chye Guan" on line 41, page 3, age 5, also from Amoy. This is a child, likely a relative or possibly a son of Lim Ah Kow. The age of 5 in 1865 suggests a birth year of approximately 1860. This is earlier than the 1872 birth record we found for Lim Chye Guan (the subject of the original request). This suggests there may be two individuals with the same name, or the family had another child named Lim Chye Guan who did not survive.

I will flag this discrepancy for Ms. Lim. It is possible that the 1872 birth record is for a second son also named Lim Chye Guan, following the naming pattern of the father and son both being named Lim Ah Kow. I will request the full manifest page to confirm the details.

---

**Entry 23 – 25 Jan 2026, 10.20 am**

Received the full manifest page for SSR-1865-014. The entry for Lim Chye Guan (line 41) shows the father's name as "Lim Ah Kow" in the remarks column. This confirms that the 5-year-old Lim Chye Guan was the son of the same Lim Ah Kow who arrived on the same ship. The family likely emigrated together.

This raises a question: if Lim Chye Guan (born ~1860) was the son of Lim Ah Kow, then the 1872 birth record for Lim Chye Guan (reg. no. 1872/0078) may refer to a different child, possibly a younger brother with the same name. The naming pattern of repeating the father's name is common, but repeating a sibling's name is less so. I will note this in the summary and suggest Ms. Lim verify with any surviving family records.
**Entry 24 – 26 Jan 2026, 9.45 am**

Spoke with Ms. Lim by phone this morning. She confirmed that the family has no surviving records of a child born around 1860. Her grandmother's notes, which she shared with me last week, list only the children born after 1870. The grandmother's notes are written in Chinese and English, with some dates that appear to be estimates. I have photographed the relevant pages and will include them in the case file.

Ms. Lim also mentioned that her great-grandfather, Lim Ah Kow, had a brother who emigrated to Penang around the same time. She does not know the brother's name. I will check the Penang records if the Singapore search does not resolve the discrepancy.

---

**Entry 25 – 26 Jan 2026, 3.15 pm**

Requested the 1872 birth register from the archives. The register is held in Series S03, Sub-series 2, which contains the Straits Settlements birth records. The reference is S03-SS2-1872-0078. The register is on microfilm and requires a reading room appointment. I have booked a slot for 28 Jan, 10.00 am.

In the meantime, I have reviewed the index for the 1872 birth register. The index lists "Lim Chye Guan" with father "Lim Ah Kow" and mother "Wong Ah Lan." The mother's name is new information. The index does not list a mother for the 1865 manifest entry, as the manifest only recorded male passengers in the remarks column with the father's name. I will note this in the summary.

---

**Entry 26 – 27 Jan 2026, 11.00 am**

Received a reply from the archives regarding my request for the full manifest of SSR-1865-014. The archives confirmed that the manifest is complete and that the entry for Lim Chye Guan (line 41) is correct. They also noted that the manifest contains a remark in the margin, written by the immigration officer, which reads: "Child's age approx; mother not on board." This remark is important. It suggests that the child's age of 5 may be an estimate, and that the mother did not travel with the family.

This changes my interpretation. If the mother was not on board, the child may have been travelling with relatives or as part of a larger group. The age of 5 may be inaccurate. I will not rely on the 1865 manifest age as a fixed birth year for Lim Chye Guan.

---

**Entry 27 – 28 Jan 2026, 10.30 am**

Reading room appointment completed. The 1872 birth register (S03-SS2-1872-0078) shows:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Name | Lim Chye Guan |
| Date of birth | 14 Mar 1872 |
| Place of birth | 12 Pagoda Street, Singapore |
| Father | Lim Ah Kow, labourer |
| Mother | Wong Ah Lan |
| Informant | Lim Ah Kow, father |
| Witness | Lee Kim Seng, neighbour |
| Remarks | None |

The register entry is clear and legible. The address, 12 Pagoda Street, matches the address on the 1874 death certificate for Lim Ah Kow (reg. no. 1874/0112). This confirms that the family lived at the same address for at least two years.

The informant is the father, which is consistent with the naming pattern. The witness, Lee Kim Seng, is listed as a neighbour. I will check if Lee Kim Seng appears in any other records in the same series.

---

**Entry 28 – 28 Jan 2026, 2.00 pm**

After the reading room, I searched the index for the 1874 death register. The entry for Lim Ah Kow (reg. no. 1874/0112) lists the cause of death as "fever" and the place of death as "12 Pagoda Street." The informant is listed as "Wong Ah Lan, wife." This is consistent with the mother's name on the 1872 birth record.

Client approved the Malacca fieldwork dates — 2024-03-11 and 12. I've sent the archive list and requested appointments. Also received confirmation from the High Court that the deed digitization is complete. The online version should be available within the week. - MC

**2024-02-13 (Tue)**
Census transcription — finished the 1891 Kallang area. Found a few more Lim families, but the records are sparse for this district. Some entries are illegible due to water damage. Will note this in the final report as a limitation. - KL

**2024-02-14 (Wed)**
Morning at the National Archives. Looked at the trade directories for 1890-1895. Found entries for Lim Ah Kow at the Balestier Road address — listed as a dealer in provisions. Also found a Lim Ah Kow at a Serangoon Road address, but the trade is listed as "general merchant." Could be the same person or a relative. Will cross-reference with the deed and the oral history. - MC

documents.title: Genealogy Research Notebook Volume 3
documents.content:
**2024-02-22 (Thu)**
Called St. Peter's Church in Malacca. The parish clerk said the 19th-century baptism registers are in the parish archive, but they are fragile and require special permission from the priest. I've emailed the priest to request access for 2024-03-12. Also, the oral history tapes have a second batch arriving next week — the vendor confirmed delivery on 2024-02-28. - MC

**2024-02-23 (Fri)**
Transcribed the fifth oral history interview — the grandson of Lim Ah Kow (interviewed 2023-11-14). He describes the Serangoon Road property as a "godown and office" used by the family trading business. He also mentions a family story that Lim Ah Kow came to Singapore from Malacca in the 1880s, after the death of his father. This aligns with the census and the deed. The Serangoon property is likely a commercial holding, not a residence. I'll flag this for the final report. - KL

**2024-02-26 (Mon)**
Dr. Tan assigned me to draft the Malacca fieldwork plan. The two-day trip is confirmed for 2024-03-11 and 12. Day 1: Cheng Hoon Teng Temple (morning) and the State Archives (afternoon). Day 2: St. Peter's Church (morning, pending priest approval) and the Malacca History Museum (afternoon). I've also added the Portuguese Settlement records as a backup if the church access falls through. - JT

**2024-02-27 (Tue)**
The second batch of oral history tapes arrived today — six more interviews. One is with a great-granddaughter of Lim Ah Kow who lives in Kuala Lumpur. She mentions a family Bible with birth and death dates, but she thinks it was lost during the Japanese occupation. Another interview is with a former neighbour from the Balestier area who remembers the shophouse in the 1950s. I'll start transcribing these tomorrow. - KL

**2024-02-28 (Wed)**
Oral history delivery confirmed — all eleven tapes received. The vendor also sent a transcript of the first five interviews, but the quality is poor (automated transcription, many errors). I'll use my own transcriptions as the primary source and note the vendor transcripts as reference only. - KL

**2024-02-29 (Thu)**
Followed up on the 1912 deed application — the High Court confirmed the digitization is complete, but the online version is not yet indexed. The clerk said it should be searchable by mid-March. In the meantime, I've requested a certified copy by mail for the client file. - MC

**2024-03-01 (Fri)**
Checked the 1901 census for the Serangoon Road area. Found a "Lim Ah Kow, age 30, general merchant, born Malacca" at a Serangoon Road address. This cannot be the same man as the Balestier household head (age 52). It's likely a son or a nephew. The age difference is too large for brothers. I'll note this as a possible family relationship but not confirm without more evidence. - KL

**2024-03-04 (Mon)**
Prepared the Malacca fieldwork kit — camera, tripod, note templates, and the archive list. Dr. Tan reviewed the plan and approved it. She reminded me to keep the fieldwork notes in the same format as the Singapore research so the final report is consistent. Also, James Lim Wei Ming serves as research_assistant on the team. Record status: current. He will be joining the Malacca trip to handle the photography and the temple records. - JT

**2024-03-05 (Tue)**
The priest at St. Peter's Church replied — permission granted for 2024-03-12, morning session, with the parish clerk present. I've confirmed the appointment. Also, the State Archives confirmed our afternoon slot. The Cheng Hoon Teng Temple is flexible. The fieldwork schedule is now fully booked. - MC

**2024-03-06 (Wed)**
Started transcribing the Kuala Lumpur interview (great-granddaughter, recorded 2023-12-02).

documents.title: Genealogy Research Notebook Volume 3
documents.content:
**2024-03-11 (Mon)**
Prepared the Malacca fieldwork binder. Included: archive list, temple contact details, map of the old town, and the consent forms (both English and Chinese versions). James confirmed he has the camera and tripod. We leave on the 13th. Dr. Tan wants a daily summary email from the field — I'll send one each evening. - MC

**2024-03-12 (Tue)**
Fieldwork day one — Malacca. Morning at St. Peter's Church. The parish clerk, Mr. Goh, was very helpful. He located the baptismal register for 1888–1892. Found the entry for "Lim Ah Kow, baptized 1890-04-15, age 24, born Malacca, merchant, sponsor: Lim Cheng Tee." This is significant — it places him in Malacca in 1890, and the sponsor may be a relative. The clerk allowed us to photograph the register page. James took high-resolution shots. Afternoon at the State Archives — we reviewed the 1891 Malacca census. Found "Lim Ah Kow, age 25, merchant, born Malacca, household head" at a Jonker Street address. This matches the baptism record. The household included his wife "Lim Neo" and a son "Lim Keng Seng, age 1." This is likely our subject's first family — need to reconcile with the Singapore records. - JT

**2024-03-13 (Wed)**
Fieldwork day two — Cheng Hoon Teng Temple. The temple's record keeper let us see the donation ledger for 1895–1905. Found "Lim Ah Kow, donated $20 for temple repairs, 1897." Also found a "Lim Keng Seng, donated $10, 1903" — possibly the son. The temple also has a list of committee members for 1900; Lim Ah Kow is listed as a committee member. This suggests he was a respected figure in the Malacca Chinese community. We photographed the relevant pages. Evening summary sent to Dr. Tan. - MC

**2024-03-14 (Thu)**
Fieldwork day three — final day in Malacca. Went back to the State Archives to check land records for Jonker Street. Found a title deed from 1892 showing "Lim Ah Kow" as the owner of a shophouse at 14 Jonker Street. The deed is in Chinese with an English translation. This matches the baptism record address. We also found a 1905 deed showing the same property transferred to "Lim Keng Seng" — likely a gift or inheritance. This is consistent with the son taking over the family property. James took photos of both deeds. We returned to Singapore in the evening. - JT

The Genealogy Research Notebook is currently on notebook_volume 3. Record status: current.

**2024-03-18 (Mon)**
Started the week by reviewing the Malacca photos. James took about 300 shots total. I've selected the clearest ones for the client file — about 40 images. I've also started a photo log with descriptions and source references. This will go into the final report appendix. - MC

**2024-03-19 (Tue)**
Checked the Singapore National Archives online portal for immigration records. The search function is limited, but I found a passenger list from 1906 showing "Lim Ah Kow, age 40, merchant, from Malacca, arriving Singapore, ship: SS Ban Hong." This fits our timeline — he moved to Singapore around 1906, after transferring the Jonker Street property to his son in 1905. This is a solid piece of evidence. I've saved the record as a PDF. - KL

**2024-03-20 (Wed)**
Followed up on the 1912 deed application. The online index is now searchable. I found the entry — the deed is for a property on Balestier Road, registered 1912-08-03, in the name of "Lim Ah Kow, merchant." This confirms he owned the Balestier shophouse from at least 1912. The certified copy should arrive by mail within two weeks. - MC

documents.title: Genealogy Research Notebook Volume 3
documents.content:

This is a significant find. I've noted the reference and will request the full record from the Malacca archives. - KL

**2024-04-01 (Mon)**
No new archival finds today. Spent the day organising the client file and updating the project timeline. The 1912 deed certified copy is now filed. I've noted this as a question to investigate. - MC

**2024-04-02 (Tue)**
Checked the Singapore Land Registry for any additional properties under Lim Ah Kow's name. Found a 1915 deed for a property on River Valley Road — registered to "Lim Ah Kow, merchant." This is new. I've noted the reference and will request the certified copy. Also checked the 1921 Straits Settlements directory — Lim Ah Kow is listed as a merchant at 14 Balestier Road. This confirms he was still active in business in the 1920s. - KL

**2024-04-03 (Wed)**
The Malacca archives responded to my request for the 1888 marriage record. They've confirmed the entry exists and will send a certified copy by post. Estimated arrival: 2-3 weeks. This will be an important piece of evidence for the report. - KL

**2024-04-08 (Mon)**
Started transcribing the 1892 Jonker Street deed from the photos. The Chinese text is difficult to read in places, but the English translation is clear. The deed describes the property as a "two-storey shophouse" and lists the boundaries. I've added the transcription to the client file. - JT

The deed is dated 1892 but appears to have been registered only in 1893. Also noted a penciled marginal annotation on the photo: "check if this is the same shophouse mentioned in the 1915 River Valley deed." I think it's a different property, but worth verifying. - JT

Drafted a preliminary family tree for the client presentation next month. The tree now includes Lim Ah Kow, his wife Tan Neo, and their children. Also added a branch for Lim Seng, Lim Ah Kow's father, based on the 1888 marriage record. - MC

**2024-04-11 (Thu)**
Spoke with the client on the phone. She mentioned an oral family tradition that Lim Ah Kow arrived in Singapore as a young man around 1870, possibly from Fujian. She's not sure of the exact village. I've noted this for further research but flagged it as unconfirmed oral history. Also asked her about the rubber trade connection; she said her grandmother used to tell stories about a "rubber estate in Johor." No documents to support this yet. - KL

**2024-04-15 (Mon)**
The Malacca archives have not yet sent the certified copy of the 1888 marriage record. I sent a follow-up email today. Also checked the National Archives of Singapore online catalogue for any Lim family files. Found a file from 1930s: "Lim Ah Kow, estate owner, correspondence regarding land dispute in Muar." This is intriguing but I need to verify whether this is the same Lim Ah Kow. The dates would make him quite old by then. - KL

**2024-04-16 (Tue)**
Requested the 1930s file from the National Archives. The reference number is NAS/1932/0451. The catalogue description mentions "dispute over boundary lines" and "rubber estate." If this is our Lim Ah Kow, it would support the rubber trade connection. I've added this to the project timeline as a pending item. - MC

**2024-04-17 (Wed)**
Received a reply from the Malacca archives. The certified copy of the 1888 marriage record has been posted and should arrive within a week. Also, I found a reference to a "Lim Ah Kow" in an 1895 issue of the Straits Times, described as "a respected member of the Chinese merchant community." I've saved the article reference. - JT

**2024-04-22 (Mon)**
The certified copy of the 1888 marriage record arrived today. It confirms the marriage of Lim Ah Kow, son of Lim Seng, and Tan Neo, daughter of Tan Kim Seng, at St. Peter's Church, Malacca, on 14 March 1888. The document also lists the witnesses: "Tan Cheng Lock" and "Lim Keng Chuan." This is excellent. I've scanned the document and filed it under "MalaccaRecords" in the shared drive. - KL

**2024-04-23 (Tue)**
Started work on the interim report. The report will cover the research progress so far, including the 1866 baptism record, the 1888 marriage record, the 1892 Jonker Street deed, and the 1915 River Valley Road deed. I've outlined the main sections: Introduction, Research Methodology, Findings, and Next Steps. I'll draft the findings section this week. - MC

**2024-04-24 (Wed)**
The National Archives confirmed the 1932 file is available for viewing. I've scheduled a visit for next Monday. Also, I checked the Singapore Land Registry again and found a 1923 deed for a property on Balestier Road, registered to "Lim Ah Kow, merchant." This is in addition to the 1921 directory listing. I've noted the reference. - KL

documents.title: Genealogy Research Notebook Volume 3
documents.content:

Drafted the Findings section of the interim report. Covered the 1866 baptism, 1888 marriage, 1892 Jonker Street deed, and 1915 River Valley Road deed. **2024-04-26 (Fri)**
Cross-checked the 1923 Balestier Road deed against the 1921 directory listing. The deed lists Lim Ah Kow as "merchant," which matches the directory. Worked on the interim report's Next Steps section. Listed the following pending items:
1. Verify the 1923 Balestier Road deed discrepancy (12 vs. 14).
2. Confirm whether the 1932 Muar land dispute involves our Lim Ah Kow.

MC reviewed the draft and suggested adding a section on the family's social connections, particularly the witnesses listed in the 1888 marriage record. Checked the Straits Times archive for the 1895 article. Started searching for immigration records for the Lim family. The family likely arrived in Singapore in the 1850s or 1860s. Checked the Straits Settlements Records index for passenger lists. Found a reference to a "Lim Ah Kow" arriving on the ship *S.S. Singapore* on 12 Mar 1865. The index entry is SSR-1865-014, series 4, item 22. I will request the full manifest from the archives.

Also noted that the National Archives has a separate collection of Chinese Protectorate records. These may contain additional immigration or registration details for the family. I will check the index for "Lim" entries in that series as well.

The manifest lists passengers on the *S.S. Singapore* departing from Amoy (Xiamen) on 28 Feb 1865 and arriving in Singapore on 12 Mar 1865.

The entry for Lim Ah Kow is on line 34, page 2. The record shows:

**Entry 22 – 24 Jan 2026, 2.30 pm**

The manifest for SSR-1865-014 also lists a "Lim Chye Guan" on line 41, page 3, age 5, also from Amoy. This is a child, likely a relative or possibly a son of Lim Ah Kow. The age of 5 in 1865 suggests a birth year of approximately 1860. This is earlier than the 1872 birth record we found for Lim Chye Guan (the subject of the original request). This suggests there may be two individuals with the same name, or the family had another child named Lim Chye Guan who did not survive.

I will flag this discrepancy for Ms. Lim. It is possible that the 1872 birth record is for a second son also named Lim Chye Guan, following the naming pattern of the father and son both being named Lim Ah Kow. I will request the full manifest page to confirm the details.

This confirms that the 5-year-old Lim Chye Guan was the son of the same Lim Ah Kow who arrived on the same ship. The family likely emigrated together.

This raises a question: if Lim Chye Guan (born ~1860) was the son of Lim Ah Kow, then the 1872 birth record for Lim Chye Guan (reg. no. 1872/0078) may refer to a different child, possibly a younger brother with the same name. This changes my interpretation. If the mother was not on board, the child may have been travelling with relatives or as part of a larger group. The age of 5 may be inaccurate. I will not rely on the 1865 manifest age as a fixed birth year for Lim Chye Guan.
